text:
Florida has gone through the season so far without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, and is still 11-7-2 with 24 points. That's the story. Paul Maurice has said both are getting close, and when they return a team already holding 53.3% of the expected goals adds its captain and its agitator.

The Panthers' record matches their chances almost exactly (24.1 expected points), and our playoff race has them at 63%. They do it the way they always have: hard, chaotic, and penalized. Florida takes 5.55 minors a game and draws 5.65, and gets 1.14 expected goals a game on the power play, which is a real weapon.

Brady Tkachuk has fit right in with his brother. The Bennett line with both Tkachuks has 57% of the expected goals, and Brady's fight with Nikita Zadorov off the opening faceoff in Boston was the loudest moment of the week. Off the ice, the brothers took heat for a Veterans Day post that was widely criticized. Sandis Vilmanis was set to return Thursday after missing time following a Tom Wilson hit that drew no suspension.

The defense holds up: Seth Jones and Niko Mikkola log the most minutes and win their share, and Aaron Ekblad with Gustav Forsling sits at 59%. They've scored 4.7 fewer goals than their chances deserved, so there's room to grow. Watch for the return dates, because this lineup gets much deeper overnight.
headline: The Panthers are surviving without Barkov and Marchand
